subject: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated capacity for Acme.ai
messages:
From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - follow up

Thanks for the call this morning, Marissa — good discussion. A couple quick clarifications from our side so we can move toward a decision: 

- Target: a real-time inference endpoint used by our customer-facing product. Peak steady-state traffic ~150 requests/sec, short bursts up to ~350 req/sec for 20-30s on launches.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120 ms end-to-end for the request/response cycle (excluding network if hosted in our primary region).
- Model: smaller Llama-style model (~7B) with cached prompts, token length typically <300 tokens.

High-level question: is Redwood Hosted API a fit for this profile, or do we need Dedicated capacity? Cost is a factor but reliability/latency is more important for us. If Dedicated, can you share sizing guidance and rough pricing?

Appreciate the quick follow-up — Sam and I are aiming to make a decision this month.

— Alex
Alex Jordan
Head of Product, Acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@acme.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - follow up

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for outlining the traffic/latency needs. Recap of our recommendation after the discovery call: 

1) Fit analysis
- Hosted API: good for bursty, low-to-moderate sustained traffic and fastest time-to-value. However, for a steady 150 req/sec with short bursts to 350 req/sec and a tight p95 <= 120 ms requirement, Hosted can work only if you accept potential variability during region-level contention and if you can tolerate conservative throttling during extreme bursts.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need predictable p95 and consistent throughput (we can size a Dedicated pool to handle steady 150 rps and absorb 350 rps bursts with predictable latency). Dedicated also gives you capacity isolation and SLA-backed latency targets.

2) Sizing guidance (preliminary)
- Based on your described model (7B, ~300 tokens, KV cache enabled), rough Dedicated sizing: 2 x A100-class equivalents with continuous autoscaling policy and a small warm margin. That would comfortably support ~200-250 sustained rps with headroom for bursts to 350 when configured with burst capacity.

3) Cost trade-offs
- Hosted: lower upfront, pay-per-use — easier to try in prod but higher unit cost at scale; variability in tail latency possible during cross-tenant contention.
- Dedicated: higher committed cost (monthly reserved), but lower unit cost and predictable latency. Also enables private VPC options later if you move toward Private.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a short throughput test plan you can run against Hosted to validate p95 under your traffic pattern. (attached: throughput_test_plan.pdf)
- If you prefer Dedicated, I'll share a preliminary pricing workbook and a formal capacity recommendation (attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx).
- Optional: schedule a technical deep-dive with Logan (runtime perf) and Dylan (capacity/pricing) to walk through benchmarks and hit a final decision.

Which path do you want to pursue this week — run a Hosted validation or move to a Dedicated sizing/pricing review? Happy to set up the deep-dive if helpful.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: throughput_test_plan.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)
From: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated - follow up

Thanks, Marissa — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups from our side: 

- We're inclined toward Dedicated given the importance of consistent p95 for the customer experience.
- Two asks before we proceed to the pricing/commit conversation: 
  1) Can Logan share a short note on expected p95 numbers (baseline) for the 7B model on the suggested Dedicated configuration? If you can include p50/p95 numbers and token-cost estimates that would be ideal.
  2) Can you also confirm whether Dedicated will give us predictable cold-start behavior for infrequent endpoints (we have a few lower-traffic event-driven endpoints)?

If you can send those two items today/tomorrow we can scope the procurement path and loop in finance. If it helps, we can take the deep-dive next week (any morning PT works).

— Sam
Sam Patel
Engineering Lead, Acme.ai
Attachments: acme-decision-summary.docx (docx, 1 page)
